Laura / Vanessa —

Thanks again for walking us through the network topology last week. Before we sign off on the BYOK handoff window we need a short checklist from Redwood that shows exactly how the keys are provisioned, where the cleartext exists (if at all), and what evidence we get for remote attestation. A couple of concrete asks from our side: 

- Definitive list of which hosts (IP ranges) will be allowed to talk to the HSM cluster and which will be denied.
- Proof artifacts for attestation (quote / signature format) and the location of that evidence for audits.
- Whether Redwood expects a privileged operator on our side during cutover or whether rotation can be fully operatorless (we prefer minimal ops).
- A short test plan we can run in our staging cage (failover + simulated node loss + kube drain) and expected post-cutover verification steps.

Also — service accounts: we need the proposed wrapping model documented. For compliance we have to show that service-account credentials are never stored in plaintext on disk and that any long-lived material is wrapped with a HSM-wrapped KEK that we control. If you can send a single PDF with the test plan + network diagram and the service-account wrapping proposal, we can schedule our acceptance window.

Thanks,
Aaron
TCI DataCenter Ops
ops@tcidc.com

Aaron —

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching three artifacts in this thread: BYOK_Test_Plan_v1.pdf, network-segmentation-edge-egress.png, and the service-account-wrap-proposal.odt. High level answers below and a proposed acceptance cadence.

Summary answers (short):
- Allowed hosts: We will publish an allowlist CIDR/hostname list for the HSM frontends; only the VPC NATs and our private peering endpoints will be allowed. No public paths. (See attachment: network diagram for CIDR blocks.)
- Attestation artifacts: Our HSMs produce a signed attestation blob (TPM-like quote) with cert chain; we will push the signed quote to a short-lived S3 bucket in your account and additionally record the signature in the audit log export.
- Operatorless rotation: Supported. We offer an operatorless rotation flow for customer-controlled KEKs where the HSM will rotate ephemeral wrapping keys on a schedule and publish wrapped-key bundles; no human operator on your side is required. We will, however, need a one-time ceremony for manual unwrapping during initial onboarding if you choose split custody.
- Staging test plan: The BYOK_Test_Plan covers failover, simulated node loss, and end-to-end wrap/unwrap. Expect ~3 hours for the full run with an optional destructive test window.

Proposed acceptance cadence:
1) You run the non-destructive staging validation (we provide a script). Completion target: May 6, 2027.
2) We run a supervised cutover in the private cage (2-hour maintenance window). Target: May 11, 2027.
3) Post-cutover audit artifacts handed to you within 24 hours.

Open question for your team: do you require HSM-backed signing of our service account JWT keys, or is wrapping with your KEK sufficient?

Action items (assigned):
- Laura: provide test artifacts and orchestration playbook (attached).
- Markus: provide the PKCS#11/KMIP compatibility matrix and the minimal API surface we'll expose to your ops team (included below).
- Vanessa: prepare the runbook and point-person list.
- Aaron: confirm acceptance window and whether you prefer a supervised (ops present) or fully automated cutover.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: TCI DataCenter Ops <ops@tcidc.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private keystore escrow acceptance and service-account wrapping

Laura / Aaron —

A few technical clarifications to make the acceptance checklist concrete (pulled from the internal compatibility matrix). Please use these as pass/fail criteria in the BYOK_Test_Plan: 

1) Protocol compatibility: We support KMIP 1.4 for key wrap/unwrapping and a PKCS#11 shim for in-process signing. If you prefer pure PKCS#11-only, we can expose that but the remote attestation plumbing (quote upload) needs the KMIP channel for metadata.

2) Service-account wrapping model (recommended):
- Long-lived service-account private keys are encrypted at creation with a customer KEK using HSM Wrap (AES-KWP).
- At runtime, tokens are minted by a Redwood short-lived signing agent which holds only ephemeral unwrapped material in memory; the signing agent returns signed JWTs over an authenticated channel.
- Optionally, we can support HSM-backed signing directly if you require key use without any intermediate agent; this increases latency but reduces trusted surface.

3) Operatorless rotation: We implement a split-custody flow where your KEK never leaves your HSM. Redwood holds an encrypted wrapped key that we rotate on a configurable cadence (default 30 days). Rotation acceptance test: request the wrapped-key bundle, perform unwrap in your environment, rewrap and confirm a rolling consumer can decrypt.

4) Audit evidence: We will ship an audit archive containing the signed attestation blobs, the key rotation event log, and the HSM cluster TLS fingerprints. For the acceptance window, expect a zipped bundle (~ < 100MB) posted to the shared bucket.

Known limitations to call out during staging:
- Offline/manual key ceremonies (emergency unseal) are still operator-assisted. We can reduce manual steps but cannot fully automate emergency split-custody evac.
- If you enable HSM-native signing, live failover may add 150–250ms per op depending on network hops.

I'll attach the technical matrix (KMIP vs PKCS11) and a minimal API spec to the Drive link.

-Markus
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Priyom —

Forwarding the thread for a short contract addendum. TCI asked us to explicitly state in writing:

- The handling of wrapped KEKs during incident response (where custody can be transferred)
- Retention window for attestation artifacts (they want 13 months)
- SLA credits if the HSM cluster experiences > 3 cumulative minutes of degraded signing across the acceptance window

I've penciled in simple language: Redwood will retain attestation artifacts for 13 months for the account, and we will provide a documented emergency custody transfer procedure (operator-assisted). For SLAs we propose: a credit eligible threshold at 30 minutes of cumulative degraded signing per month.

Please review and advise if we can sign off without legal escalation.

Thanks —
Laura
